nodes.title: Round d35 merged: the dry matrix exits 0 on nine topics (36 lessons) after three merges, a follow-up and a closing pass; 532 counts moved, each attributed to a stage

A question is said at most four times, and the cap fires only where she would say it again on her own (after a miss, a give-up or no answer): a child's own request for the question is always honoured; the short ask and the invitation are not hearings
A child's own step posed on the worked example's board may show its answer on a different figure after the answer; the checker's same-figure rule holds only where the step has a board of its own
fraction-line@1 accepts a mixed-number label whose value equals its mark ("1 3/4", "7/4 = 1 3/4"), and the checker reads it as drawing its parts
A child whose answer is a wrongAnswers entry hears that answer's reason, then the hint, then the key, and is never sent to the card's remediation; a check may carry targets with no wrongIfMis
The script grade matches each number's unit (the first unit said after it): a unit that contradicts the key's is a different answer; a bare number still matches
The checker refuses a re-ask equal to its prompt's last sentence, and a re-ask is required on every card, follow-up card and own step
An aside parked at the closing question goes as at a card (park line, the question or the pointed invitation, the board kept); the wrap opens on the library's reply to a held return
Every bridge between skills carries an easier wording: help at a bridge's check-in is that sentence, then the same check-in; main wrote the two the ninth script lacked

The checker's new rule (a stated value must be drawn) met its old one (an answer board is the posing figure) and authors satisfied both by posing steps on the answer's own figure: three worked examples gave their step away, one board wrote the named mistake, one drew a wrong answer as true; every one was found by the cold read, none by the checker

The first build of the four-hearings cap counted and capped every hearing, so a worked step was told to a child who had only said "Hindi mein bolo" or "haan" (six told steps and two broken Hindi requests on the dry matrix)

Requiring a re-ask on every card produced four re-asks that were their card's own last sentence; the cold reads and the checker passed them, the dry predicates on the merged tree caught two and a new checker rule the other two

Authors named wrong answers at volume from judgement, not from children (25 on 21 cards in one script, 14 in another, none heard in a run): cold readers judged most typical and found six reasons faulty (one gave the key, one false, four spoke to something the child did not do)

Three check cards routed a named wrong answer to a remediation about a different mistake (the fault judges heard as 'wrong on twelfths, re-taught halves'), and neither the loader nor the checker allows a check without a target
Counting a child's own request for the question toward the cap and capping on it: the fifth hearing told the step to a child who asked for Hindi

Giving a child's own step a posing board that is its answer board unmarked, to satisfy 'a stated value must be drawn': the unmarked figure shows the answer's shape (five parts, 21 dots, a 7-part strip)
Removing a check's targets so a named wrong answer is not sent to an unfitting remediation: refused by the loader and the checker in three scripts
Comparing the units of a compound quantity as a set: "7 metre 50 metre" graded right against 7 metre 50 centimetre

md.measurements: - `ms-r8-d35-merged-dry` (2026-11-24): the dry matrix (no model; reactive rule-based child; four children per topic; seven live topics and two staged, 36 lessons) on the merged round-d35 tree. **At the engine merge with the scripts of before the round** (run m1): staged exit 0; live exit 1 on one row (steady c5-ch02-t03 82: an aside at the closing question cleared the board, so the help page that followed was drawn at the turn's start), fixed in the follow-up (58b89692e: an aside at the closing question goes as an aside at a card). **Fully merged** (run m2, a764ca143 + 418da7e15): three gated flags, all one cause: two re-asks that were their card's own last sentence (c5-t01 s1 remediation[1].then, c6-ch07-t03 s2 e3), heard as the question twice running; main reworded them, the checker then refused that shape and found two more (c5-t01 s3 c3, s3 remediation[1].then). **Final** (run close2, tree of 06b1ac3aa): check exit 0 live and staged, every gated predicate 0, the eleven new ones included (the no-other-drawing line while the hint owns an unsaid board; that line then only an invitation while a wording is unsaid; a picture taken down by that line; a first give-up at a bridge's check-in that goes on; the card whole after try-first or a bare yes; a question a fifth time on her own; a right close that cannot share its turn ending on a check-in; a Hindi request at a card with no form ending on a check-in; a code-added "Suno,"/"Dekho," after a verdict; an aside reply of another kind; a named reason to a child who did not give that answer). Counted, not gated: reasonTwiceAuthored 6, cardNoFit 5, vpcWhole 5, repeatedAuthored 4, pointNoFit 4, workedNoFit 2. Picture requests, 45: the board's second view 19, the card's authored picture 13, the no-other-drawing line then the hint in words 8, the hint's own board drawn 4, the line and an invitation 1 (all spent). Turn endings: the invitation 105 (at most 7 in a lesson; 88 and 5 in round d34's final dry run), the pointed invitation 8, the short ask 25, the try-first line alone 30; the easier-words line 5. The four-hearings cap fired 11 times (a key with its reason, or a told step). First give-up at a bridge's check-in helped 6 of 6; the one second give-up went on. A `wrongAnswers` reason said 5 times; 24 of 36 dry children gave such an answer at some card (most got the hint or the key there: the reason is said once, after the miss, where help is next). Check-in endings in steady lessons: 5, 4, 3, 3, 3, 3, 4 live and 3, 3 staged (3, 3, 3, 3, 2, 2, 3 and 2, 3 in d34). Longest turn 74 words, 20 over 70. The counts baseline (evals/hybrid-side-by-side/counts-baseline.json) was rewritten once, on the final run's live seven: 532 counts moved against the baseline of to-brain 052 E, attributed by running the dry matrix at each of twelve stage commits with each stage's own scripts (the first stage reproduces the old baseline exactly). Grader gate on the nine scripts with `wrongAnswers` read: 74 cards, 337 forms, none failed. Script checker: all nine pass plain, `--standard --d32 --d33 --d34`, and `--d35`. Tests: `npm run test:all` on 72516544d: 816 suites, 8,068 tests, 8,046 pass, 7 fail in 6 suites, 13 skipped, 2 todo; all seven were this round's (six re-pins to the round's script and reply-library changes, and one predicate, closeNoFitCheckin, that flagged scripts with no plain go-on form), fixed in 91f97f4fb and 8bb1bf364 and re-run in their files (109 of 109); the whole suite was not run locally a second time (CI runs it on the release candidate). `npx tsc -b`, `npx vite build` and the prompt budget pass; the final dry run re-checked with the amended predicate: exit 0, same lines. n = 36 dry lessons; method: `scratchpad/d35/a/run.sh`, `evals/hybrid-side-by-side/check-run.mjs`, `scripts/judge-prompt-check.mjs --endings`, the closing builder's facts script; not measured: any of this with a model or a child (director35 is that).
md.decisions:
- `dc-r8-four-hearings-cap-on-her-own-repeat` (2026-11-24, main, refines `dc-r8-director34` item 6): every turn that says a card's or an asked step's question in any form counts toward four; a fifth that she would say **on her own** (after a miss, a give-up or no answer) is the key with its reason, or the step told. A child's own request for the question (a Hindi request, "phir se bolo") is always honoured whatever the count; a bare "haan", a try-first and an aside never trigger the cap; the short ask and the invitation are not hearings. **Why:** the first build capped every fifth hearing and told a step to a child who had asked for Hindi (`fd-r8-cap-told-a-step-at-a-request`). **Reverses if** two judges hear a question more than six times in a lesson because requests do not cap; then requests get a cap of their own that ends on help, never on the key.
- `dc-r8-own-step-answer-on-another-figure` (2026-11-24, main, refines Learning 023 rule 1): where a worked example's own step has no board of its own it is posed on the worked board (or the last step's result board) and its `answerBoard` may be any figure, drawn at the close; rule 1 reads the step's reason and the worked answer over it. Where the step has its own board the old rule stands (the answer board is that figure, marked). **Why:** `fd-r8-drawn-value-rule-forced-giveaway-boards`. **Reverses if** judges in two topics count the change of figure at an own step's close as a contradiction or hear the child lost by it; then the worked board's template learns to carry the answer mark and the figure stays.
- `dc-r8-number-line-writes-a-mixed-number` (2026-11-24, main): `fraction-line@1` accepts a label that is a mixed number, alone or either side of "=", when its value equals the mark; the checker reads such a label as drawing the whole, the fraction and the improper fraction. **Why:** `c5-maths-ch02-t01` s3's own step could only satisfy rule 1 by writing "3/4" at 0.75, before 1, which is the card's named wrong answer. **Reverses if** the label does not fit at phone width on a judged run; then it breaks onto two lines in the template.
- `dc-r8-named-answer-skips-the-remediation` (2026-11-24, main, refines `dc-r8-director34` item 5): an answer named in `wrongAnswers` gets its own reason once, then the card's hint, then the key; the walk does not route that child to the remediation the card targets. Three checks moved their `wrongIfMis` into `wrongAnswers` for this (`c4-maths-ch05-t01` s1 c2, `c4-maths-ch01-t02` s3 c2, `c5-maths-ch02-t03` s1 c2); loader and checker accept a check with `targets` and no `wrongIfMis` when it has a `wrongAnswers` entry. **Why:** `fd-r8-misrouted-named-answer`. **Reverses if** the learner model is shown to lose evidence it needs (a named answer that is the targeted misconception recorded with no misconception id); then a `wrongAnswers` entry may carry an id of its own and still skip the remediation.
- `dc-r8-units-matched-to-their-numbers` (2026-11-24, main): in `server/grading/script-answer.js` each number's unit is the first unit said after it; two answers differ when a number's units disagree, or when one side gives a bare number a unit it already used for another number. About 5,700 forms graded before and after: every change is right → not right, all of the shape "7 metre 50 metre". **Reverses if** a right spoken form is graded wrong for its unit order on a judged run; then quantities are compared by their total in one unit.
- `dc-r8-reask-is-not-its-cards-last-sentence` (2026-11-24, main): under `--d35` a `reask` is required on every card, follow-up card and own step, and one equal (after normalisation) to its prompt's last sentence is an error. **Why:** `fd-r8-reask-equal-to-its-question`. **Reverses if** authors answer it with re-asks longer than their questions; then the rule also caps the re-ask at its prompt's last sentence's length.
- `dc-r8-aside-at-the-closing-question-as-at-a-card` (2026-11-24, main): an aside parked at the closing question gets the park line and the question (its re-ask once said; the pointed invitation on the third turn at it), with the board kept; the wrap opens on the reply library's form for a held return. A repeated aside or a question about her own taste there still gets the old free line. **Reverses if** a judge quotes that free line at the closing question as a turn that does not say the question; then those two paths go the same way.
- `dc-r8-every-bridge-has-an-easier-wording` (2026-11-24, main): to-brain 053 B1 helps a first give-up or "samajh nahi aaya" at a bridge's check-in with the bridge's own `simpler`, then the same check-in; a second goes on. Eight of the nine scripts have carried a `simpler` on every bridge since director22 (2a4d7e8be); the staged c6-maths-ch07-t03 had none, so its first give-up went on with no help where the closed card's reason had just been said, and main wrote its two (06b1ac3aa). Main had first recorded, from one builder's line about that one script, that no bridge had one, and wrote the judges' rule K4(a), clause 58 and the not-built list on it; reading the dry rows against the prompt before the run caught it. **Reverses if** clause 58 of director35 fires: a first give-up at a check-in answered by the go-on line alone (walk fault), or the easier wording heard as the bridge again in two lessons (Learning rewrites them, read cold).
md.rejected:
- `rj-r8-cap-that-counts-and-caps-requests` (2026-11-24): **tried** to-brain 053 B3 as first written ("the Hindi form said at the child's request counts", and a fifth hearing is the key or the step told). **What broke:** the fifth hearing could be the child's own request: on the dry matrix a worked step was told at "Hindi mein bolo", at a bare "haan" and at an aside (six `stepToldEarly` rows, two `hindiNoFormNoLine`). The predicates were right. **Now:** `dc-r8-four-hearings-cap-on-her-own-repeat`.
- `rj-r8-own-step-posed-on-its-answer-figure` (2026-11-24): **tried** meeting Learning 023 rule 1 at a child's own step by giving the step a posing board that is its answer board without the mark (the checker required the two to be one figure). **What broke:** the unmarked figure is most of the answer: two strips of 6 and 5 parts after the step that rules out 6 (`c6-maths-ch07-t01` s1), 21 countable dots under "3 × 7 = ?" and an empty 7-part strip for 2/7 (`c6-maths-ch07-t03`). **Now:** `dc-r8-own-step-answer-on-another-figure`.
- `rj-r8-dropping-targets-to-stop-a-misroute` (2026-11-24): **tried** removing `targets` from a check whose named wrong answer is sent to a remediation about another mistake. **What broke:** the runtime loader and the checker both require every check to target a kit misconception (three fixers hit it independently). **Now:** the answer moves to `wrongAnswers`, which the walk does not route (`dc-r8-named-answer-skips-the-remediation`).
- `rj-r8-units-compared-as-a-set` (2026-11-24): **tried** (as built since 050) comparing the units of a spoken quantity as a set. **What broke:** "7 metre 50 metre" equals the accepted "7 metre 50" and grades right where the key is 7 metre 50 centimetre; found by a fixer's grading probe, never by a run. **Now:** `dc-r8-units-matched-to-their-numbers`.
